title: How to Find Pay Per Call Clients and Buyers
h1: How to find pay per call clients and buyers
description: Where to find pay per call buyers, how to pitch them and what they check before they sign: a practical guide for publishers and new networks.
faq: Where do pay per call buyers come from?

Most buyers are businesses that close sales on the phone, such as home-service companies, law firms and insurance agencies, plus networks and call centers that resell calls. You can reach them directly, through networks and marketplaces, at industry events and on LinkedIn.
What do buyers want to see before they buy calls?
Clear rules for what counts as a billable call, proof of call quality such as recordings, respect for their hours and daily caps, and a simple way to see the calls they were charged for.
Should I start with a network or go direct to buyers?
Many publishers start with a network because the buyers, rules and payments are already in place, then add direct buyers once they have steady volume and want a higher payout per call.
body:
To find pay per call clients, start with businesses that already close sales on the phone and buy customers every month: home-service companies, law firms, insurance agencies and the networks and call centers that serve them. Reach them where they already look for calls, show them exactly what a billable call is, and make it easy for them to check every call they pay for. The rest of this guide covers where to look, how to pitch and what buyers check before they say yes.

Who buys pay per call traffic

A pay per call buyer is any business that earns more from a phone call than it pays for it. They usually fall into four groups:

  • Local service businesses such as plumbers, roofers, HVAC and pest control companies, who pay for callers that need a job done. See home services pay per call.
  • Law firms, especially personal injury firms, who pay for callers with a case in the states where they practise. See legal pay per call.
  • Insurance and financial agencies selling final expense, Medicare, health or debt relief, who pay for callers in states where they are licensed.
  • Networks, marketplaces and call centers that buy calls in volume and resell or work them across many end buyers.

If you are new to the model, our guide to what pay per call is explains how publishers, affiliates and buyers fit together.

Where to find pay per call clients

1. Go direct to businesses that answer the phone

Search for the businesses in your vertical and area, check that they take calls during clear opening hours, and contact the owner or marketing lead. Smaller local buyers often have never bought calls before, so explain the model in one sentence: they pay only for calls that meet agreed rules.

2. Join pay per call networks and marketplaces

Networks already have buyers with set prices and rules. Joining one gives you buyers on day one while you learn which verticals convert for your traffic. Later, you can approach end buyers directly for higher payouts.

3. Use LinkedIn the right way

Buyers post on LinkedIn every week when they need more calls, often with the verticals, call length and payout range they accept. Search posts for terms such as "buying inbound calls" or "publishers needed" in your vertical, then reply with what you can deliver, not a generic pitch.

4. Go to industry events

Lead generation and affiliate conferences such as LeadsCon and Affiliate Grand Slam bring buyers, networks and publishers into one room. Book meetings before the event and bring a one-page summary of your traffic sources and verticals.

5. Ask existing buyers for referrals

A buyer who is happy with your calls often knows others in the same industry who need volume. Ask once you have a few weeks of clean results.

How to pitch a pay per call buyer

  1. Lead with their rules, not your traffic. Ask which states, hours, call length and daily cap they need, then show how you will meet them.
  2. Offer a small test. A short test with a low daily cap lets the buyer judge quality with little risk.
  3. Agree what a billable call is in writing. Minimum duration, allowed states, duplicate rules and how disputes are settled.
  4. Show them how they will check calls. Buyers trust publishers who give them their own view of calls, answer rates and charges.

What buyers check before they sign

  • Call quality: recordings and short summaries so they can review calls quickly.
  • Rules respected on every call: hours, caps and states checked before a call rings, and repeat callers blocked.
  • Clear reporting: every call they received, how many they answered and what they were charged.
  • Consistent volume: steady calls within their cap, not a flood one day and nothing the next.
